ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given in the figure, points B, D, and C lie on a straight line, with AB = AD, AC = AE, and $\angle BAD = \angle CAE$. If $\angle B = 65^\circ$ and BC = DE, what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=AD$ and $\angle B=65^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle B=65^\circ$, \\
since $\triangle BAC \cong \triangle DAE$, \\
it implies that $\angle ADE=\angle B=65^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle CDE=180^\circ-\angle ADE-\angle ADB \\
=180^\circ-2\times65^\circ \\
=\boxed{50^\circ}.$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given in the figure, points B, D, and C lie on a straight line, with AB = AD, AC = AE, and $\angle BAD = \angle CAE$. If $\angle B = 65^\circ$ and BC = DE, what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?

Image description: In the figure, B, D, and C are located on the same bottom straight line, with D between B and C; A is at the upper left, and E is at the upper right. The figure shows line segments such as AB, AD, AC, AE, and DE, and DB and DC starting from D are opposite-direction rays on the same straight line.

Reasoning: Since the problem gives AB = AD, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, so the base angles are equal, that is, ∠ABD = ∠ADB. Because B, D, and C are collinear, ∠B in the figure is ∠ABC, and is also the same as ∠ABD. It is known that ∠B = 65°, so ∠ADB = 65°.

Also, from AB = AD, AC = AE, and BC = DE, it can be obtained that triangles BAC and DAE have three corresponding sides equal, therefore △BAC ≅ △DAE (SSS). Thus the corresponding angles ∠ABC = ∠ADE. Also ∠ABC = ∠B = 65°, so ∠ADE = 65°.

At point D, DB and DC form a straight line, therefore the sum of the three adjacent angles above, ∠ADB, ∠ADE, and ∠CDE, is 180°. So ∠CDE = 180° - 65° - 65° = 50°.
